overview.title: Oversight
overview.summary: Explore who has authority, or start with a question and walk through an investigation. Open a connector to see the decision that permits the next step.
choices: Start with a legislative purpose and identify the chamber, committee and official with authority.
Start with an answerable question. Establish what the records support before assigning a role to anyone.
Use historical records to identify specific failure points and test proposed safeguards.

decisions.title: Authorized decisions
decisions.summary: The evidence can support a legislative response, a separately authorized state referral, both, or neither.
facts: A reviewer has checked what the evidence establishes, what is disputed and what remains unknown. Counsel checks each proposed use and disclosure.
The official or body with authority under the applicable chamber and committee rules approves congressional action. A receiving state office exercises its own authority.
Record the evidence gap, jurisdiction problem or disclosure restriction. Narrow the finding, keep investigating within authority, or close the matter as appropriate.
choices: The authorized committee approves an action within its jurisdiction using findings the record can support.
Proceed on a separate state-law basis after verifying the recipient, screening each item and obtaining disclosure approval. State review is optional.

congressional-action.title: Congressional action
congressional-action.summary: Congress can act on a supported legislative finding without waiting for federal prosecution or a state referral.
facts: Consider an authorized hearing, report, audit request, legislative proposal or appropriations follow-up. Use the applicable chamber and committee process.
Clear the facts, scope and permitted disclosures before release. Label unresolved questions and preserve contrary evidence and corrections.
Name the owner and review date. Track the legislative response separately from a referral, an investigation, any charges and a disposition.
choices: Reopen evidence review if new records, contradictions or corrections change what the finding supports.
